task: Phase 12 backlog item (master_agnostic_tasks.md line 104): re-check large-book project/chapter load timings. Measured against the largest real project on disk (28 chapters / ~730K chars of text_content) via curl against a locally-run backend pointed at the real DB. The Contents-view list endpoint was already fast; found and fixed a real redundant-refetch bug in the chapter editor's loader instead.

app/db/chapters.py.summary: get_chapter() now runs the same total_segments_count/done_segments_count subqueries as list_chapters() (previously only the list endpoint computed these), so single-chapter callers get the same shape as the list endpoint. No API contract change — these are additive fields on an existing response, and the chapter editor UI already reads them from `chapter.total_segments_count`/`done_segments_count` (ChapterWorkspaceHeader, ChapterTextPanel's analysisChapter fallback) so this fixes a pre-existing gap where the single-chapter endpoint silently omitted them.

frontend/src/hooks/chapter/useChapterLoa.summary: loadChapter() now calls api.fetchChapter(chapterId) (GET /api/chapters/{id}, ~700B/~4ms) instead of api.fetchChapters(projectId) + Array.find (GET /api/projects/{id}/chapters, ~780KB/~60-100ms for the measured 28-chapter book — the full list including every OTHER chapter's full text_content). This loader runs on mount, on every websocket chapter-update/segment-update tick, and on every 1s completion-poll tick (up to 30x per render), so the old code re-transferred the whole project's chapter text repeatedly just to read one chapter's fields. Minor behavior note: the single-chapter endpoint doesn't cross-check project_id the way `chapters.find(c => c.id === chapterId)` implicitly did — not exercised by real navigation (chapterId is always routing-scoped) so left as-is.

flow_impact: No flow/invariant shape change. list_chapters() (used by Book Contents/ProjectDetail chapter lists) is untouched. get_chapter()'s new fields are additive and match an existing shape consumers already expect. The only behavioral change is which HTTP endpoint the chapter editor's background loader calls — same data reaches the same state setters (setChapter/setTitle/setText/setLocalVoice), just without the other chapters' text riding along.
